messages:
deploy-bot: :rotating_light: Deploy to prod started: rollout ae3f9 -> canary at 10% (region: us-west1). Notifying @carol on-call.

carol (oncall): saw a spike in errors hitting the canary. page triggered by incident-bot. jumping in.

incident-bot: Alert: Elevated 5xx rate on /v1/generate (canary nodes). 5xx rate increased from 0.2% baseline to 6.8% over the last 5m. p95 latency climbed from ~120ms -> 3.2s, p99 -> 8.9s.

alice (sre): @carol I'm attaching quick traces — looks like requests are stalling during KV cache warmup and long batching windows. Possibly the new batching heuristic in ae3f9 is holding requests open.

bob (eng-runtime): I rolled a small change into ae3f9 that adjusts dynamic_batcher timeout from 20ms -> 200ms for 'longer' sequences. That was intended to improve throughput but could increase tail latency if traffic mix changes.

carol (oncall): Can someone confirm whether only canary traffic is affected? Is this across all models or a specific model variant?

dave (prod-ops): Support reporting a handful of customer escalations in the last 10m — some requests timing out client-side. Not many but noisy. Erin, any customer-facing impact quant yet?

erin (support): ~12 unique tenants hit timeouts so far, mostly long-sequence generation (>1k tokens). No degradation reported on embeddings endpoints.

alice (sre): Running `rwb metrics query --service inference --q 'status:5xx,env:prod,revision:ae3f9' --range 5m` shows 5xx spike concentrated on canary hosts. Rollout is at 10% so global impact limited but visible on SLAs.

alice (sre): quick logs: ```
[2026-03-14T12:03:21Z] node-canary-3 runtime: batch_wait hit 200ms, KV-miss, stall for pending KV fetch
[2026-03-14T12:03:22Z] node-canary-1 runtime: request timeout -> upstream 504 after 6s
[2026-03-14T12:03:23Z] node-canary-2 runtime: long queue depth detected, batch size 128 -> 512
```

bob (eng-runtime): Ugh, that explains it. The heuristic increases max batch size when it sees more long sequences, but we missed bounding combined latency. For canary traffic (10% mix) it pushed some requests into huge batches that then blocked on kv cache seeding.

carol (oncall): Given customer-visible timeouts, recommend aborting canary and rolling back ae3f9 to ae3e4 (previous stable). Thoughts?

dave (prod-ops): +1. Customer impact non-negligible and root cause linked to batching heuristic. Abort canary and rollback. Prepare public note if rollback doesn't clear within 15m.

alice (sre): Initiating rollback. Command: `rwb rollout abort --target canary --revision ae3f9` then `rwb deploy --env prod --revision ae3e4 --strategy immediate`

deploy-bot: Rollout abort acknowledged. Canary flagged for rollback. Starting deployment of ae3e4 to replace canary nodes. Estimated completion ~3m.

incident-bot: Automated mitigation: routing policy switched to prefer stable model variants for 100% of routing. Circuit breaker engaged on canary nodes: max in-flight per-host lowered to 16.

carol (oncall): Monitoring: within 90s we see 5xx rate dropping on global ingress. p95 back to ~150ms, p99 trending down to ~400ms.

erin (support): No new customer escalations in the last 5m. Previous ones are being updated with workaround (retry with short backoff).

alice (sre): Post-rollback checks: KV cache hit rates returning to baseline, batch sizes normalized. Confirming `rwb metrics` shows 5xx back to 0.4% and error budget not impacted beyond canary window.

bob (eng-runtime): I'll open a PR to add an upper bound on dynamic batch growth and add an opt-in flag for long-sequence aggressive batching. Also will add a canary flag to disable the heuristic by default during staged rollouts.

dave (prod-ops): Good. Action items: 1) rollback complete, 2) revert heuristic in next patch, 3) run targeted load-tests for long-seq paths, 4) postmortem and customer impact summary. Assigning owners: bob -> code patch, alice -> rollout verification + telemetry, carol -> incident writeup + oncall notes, dave -> customer communications.

carol (oncall): Handing off to alice for follow-up and postmortem. I'm going offline for next 2h but will ping if something regresses. @alice please escalate if rollback doesn't stabilise.

alice (sre): Will take over. Adding timeline to incident doc and kicking off postmortem board. Quick summary to put in incident tracker: "Canary deployment ae3f9 increased dynamic batching windows, causing oversized batches on long-seq requests which led to KV cache stalls and elevated p99/timeouts. Canary aborted and rollback to ae3e4 restored baseline."

erin (support): I'll prepare a customer-facing timeline and list of affected tenants. ETA 30m for initial note.

dave (prod-ops): :thumbsup: Great work. Closing on-call loop. We'll mark Sev-2 and follow up with a detailed postmortem.

incident-bot: Incident status changed -> Mitigated. Handed off to alice (sre) for post-incident review.

alice (sre): Logged follow-up tasks in backlog and scheduled postmortem meeting for tomorrow 09:30 PT.

carol (oncall): :white_check_mark: leaving handoff.
